response.answer:
For 4 days of RV dry camping at a festival with no generator, I'd recommend a combination of lithium batteries + solar panels, sized according to whether you need air conditioning.

The biggest question is whether you want to run the RV's A/C. That changes the power requirements dramatically.

Recommended power setup for 4 days

Air conditioning for several hours daily

	

15–30+ kWh

	

1,000W+

These are starting estimates, not guaranteed four-day runtimes. Solar output depends on weather, shade, and panel placement.

Three ways to power your RV
Shop

1. Portable power station

Easiest option. A 4–8 kWh expandable system can power many everyday RV needs. Look for an RV-compatible output, sufficient inverter capacity, and solar charging.

Shop

2. Built-in lithium battery system

Best for frequent boondocking. Install LiFePO4 batteries, a suitable inverter/charger, solar controller, and properly protected wiring.

Shop

3. Portable solar panels

Useful for replenishing batteries during the festival. A 600W array might produce roughly 1.5–2.5 kWh on a reasonably sunny day, depending on conditions.

Important: A standard RV rooftop A/C often consumes around 1,200–1,800W while running. Even a 10 kWh battery could be depleted in roughly 5–8 hours of continuous A/C use, before accounting for other loads and inverter losses.

markup:
For **4 days of RV dry camping at a festival with no generator**, I'd recommend a combination of **lithium batteries + solar panels**, sized according to whether you need air conditioning.

The biggest question is whether you want to run the RV's A/C. That changes the power requirements dramatically.

## Recommended power setup for 4 days

| What you want to power | Battery capacity | Solar |
|---|---|---|
| Lights, phone charging, water pump, fridge on propane | 2–3 kWh | 200–400W |
| Above + TV, fans, laptops, electric fridge | 4–6 kWh | 400–800W |
| Above + microwave, coffee maker, occasional high-power appliances | 6–10 kWh | 600–1,200W |
| Air conditioning for several hours daily | 15–30+ kWh | 1,000W+ |

These are starting estimates, not guaranteed four-day runtimes. Solar output depends on weather, shade, and panel placement.

## Three ways to power your RV

  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 portable power station" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="136px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **1. Portable power station**

      Easiest option. A 4–8 kWh expandable system can power many everyday RV needs. Look for an RV-compatible output, sufficient inverter capacity, and solar charging.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="RV LiFePO4 lithium battery bank solar inverter installation" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="136px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **2. Built-in lithium battery system**

      Best for frequent boondocking. Install LiFePO4 batteries, a suitable inverter/charger, solar controller, and properly protected wiring.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align=start gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="RV portable folding solar panels camping setup" aspectRatio="1:1" maxWidth="136px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **3. Portable solar panels**

      Useful for replenishing batteries during the festival. A 600W array might produce roughly 1.5–2.5 kWh on a reasonably sunny day, depending on conditions.
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

**Important:** A standard RV rooftop A/C often consumes around 1,200–1,800W while running. Even a 10 kWh battery could be depleted in roughly 5–8 hours of continuous A/C use, before accounting for other loads and inverter losses.

## Calculate your 4-day battery needs

{@body const [daily,setDaily] = DIL.useState(1.5)}
{@body const [solar,setSolar] = DIL.useState(400)}
{@body const solarDaily = solar*4*0.75/1000}
{@body const required = Math.max(0,(daily-solarDaily)*4/0.85)}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      **Daily electricity consumption**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{daily.toFixed(1)} kWh</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={0.5} max={12} step={0.5} value={daily} onChange={setDaily}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      **Solar panel capacity**
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{solar} W</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={0} max={1600} step={100} value={solar} onChange={setSolar}/>
  </box>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Estimated battery capacity needed</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{required.toFixed(1)} kWh</title>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Estimated solar production/day</text>
      <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{solarDaily.toFixed(1)} kWh</title>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <caption>Illustrative calculation assuming four peak-sun-hours daily, 75% solar system efficiency, and 85% usable battery capacity. Actual results vary, especially with festival shade and weather.</caption>
</box>

## A couple of questions

{@body const [ac,setAc] = DIL.useState("no")}
{@body const [fridge,setFridge] = DIL.useState("propane")}
{@body const [budget,setBudget] = DIL.useState("1000-2500")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("For my 4-day RV festival dry camping setup: A/C: "+ac+". Fridge: "+fridge+". Budget: "+budget+". Recommend a specific battery and solar setup.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Will you need air conditioning?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={ac} onChange={setAc}>
        <radio value="no">No, just fans and normal RV appliances</radio>
        <radio value="day">Yes, a few hours during the day</radio>
        <radio value="night">Yes, overnight</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What type of refrigerator?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={fridge} onChange={setFridge}>
        <radio value="propane">Propane / electric</radio>
        <radio value="12v">12V electric</radio>
        <radio value="residential">Residential 120V refrigerator</radio>
        <radio value="unknown">Not sure</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What's your budget for power?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={budget} onChange={setBudget}>
        <radio value="under-1000">Under $1,000</radio>
        <radio value="1000-2500">$1,000–$2,500</radio>
        <radio value="2500-5000">$2,500–$5,000</radio>
        <radio value="5000+">$5,000+</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Recommend my setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

With those answers, I can narrow it down to a practical setup that lasts the full four days without running a generator.
